about: DNA-origami designs of the Nanorulers specimen (BSD-3-Clause). tools/gen_origami_designs.mjs validates them and builds the JS reference's table (web/prototype/scope/origami_designs_data.js) and the core's (core/src/origami_designs.inc); never edit those by hand. A design's index here is the core param origamiDesign.

A design is the molecule at rest: a body in its own straight frame (x along the length from -L/2 to L/2, y across it in the coverslip plane, h the height relative to the body's axis), the spots of docking strands on it (a ring of n strand positions around the body, or a strand list), how it deforms (wlc2d: the centreline is a 2D surface-equilibrated worm-like chain of persistence length Lp, cross-sections stay straight and normal to it; rigid: none) and how it lands (roll about its own axis: uniform or fixed; the height of the body's bottom above the glass).

Per molecule: rest sites -> incorporation (the label's labelling %) -> deformation -> landing (roll, heights) -> placement (position, yaw) -> emitters; every step a pure function of (seed, address). 'deformation' and 'landing' values are the suggested defaults of the origami* params (the params win).

Implemented (v1): body 'cylinder', deformation 'wlc2d' and 'rigid', roll 'uniform' and 'fixed', spots with a ring. Reserved, validated as not implemented: bodies 'cuboid', 'mesh'; deformation 'wlc3d', 'plate'; stiffnessVariation and curvaturePerUm != 0; explicit strand lists ('strands').

designs.name: 80 nm nanoruler
designs.notes: The typical nanoruler body, a 12-helix bundle about 200 nm long and 13 nm in diameter (scheckenbach2020), as a cylinder, with three spots of docking strands 80 nm apart at 20, 100 and 180 nm from one end; five strand positions per spot, 72 deg apart on the surface (a modelling choice, not a product's specification). Persistence length 1500 nm: an estimate, softer than the 3-8.2 um measured for eight-helix bundles (chhabra2020). Geometry and bending: tools/origami_reference/origami_bend.py.
